sections.heading: C — Graduated driver license program
sections.markdown:
## C — Graduated driver license program

FACT_ID: sec02-F01 | anchor: A01
Everyone who obtains a learner's permit or a junior driver's license in Vermont is subject to the graduated driver's license law [A01].
Why it matters: The law attaches to both provisional documents, not only the junior license.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec02-F02 | anchor: A01
Under the graduated license law a person fifteen or older may operate a vehicle on a valid learner's permit only when a qualified person rides beside the driver: a licensed, unimpaired parent or guardian, a licensed or certified and unimpaired driver education instructor, or a licensed, unimpaired person at least twenty-five years old [A01].
Why it matters: The supervisor must sit beside the driver, and must be unimpaired.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec02-F03 | anchor: A01
An applicant for a learner's permit must have kept a clean driving record during the previous two years [A01].
Why it matters: A two year clean record is required before the very first permit.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec02-F04 | anchor: A01
A learner's permit must be held for at least one year before a junior driver's license can be obtained [A01].
Why it matters: One full year on the permit is a fixed minimum.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec02-F05 | anchor: A01
Before getting a junior driver's license the permit holder must complete an additional forty hours of practice behind the wheel, at least ten of them nighttime driving, with a qualified supervisor riding beside the driver who then certifies the practice [A01].
Why it matters: Practice must be both supervised and certified.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec02-F06 | anchor: A01
The forty practice hours come on top of the six hours of behind the wheel instruction in a driver training course, and nighttime driving for this purpose means the period from thirty minutes after sunset to thirty minutes before sunrise [A01].
Why it matters: Course instruction hours and practice hours are separate totals.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec02-F07 | anchor: A01
A junior driver's license requires a clean record with no learner's permit recalls, suspensions or revocations during the six months before it is obtained [A01].
Why it matters: The six month clean window is counted right before the junior license.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec02-F08 | anchor: A01
For one year after a junior driver's license is issued the holder may not drive a vehicle as part of a job, such as delivering pizza, until that year passes or the holder reaches eighteen, whichever comes first [A01].
Why it matters: Turning eighteen ends the employment driving ban early.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec02-F09 | anchor: A01
A junior driver's license holder may not carry passengers for hire [A01].
Why it matters: Paid passengers are barred for the whole junior license period.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec02-F10 | anchor: A01
During the first three months of driving on a junior driver's license the holder is restricted to driving alone, and passengers are allowed only when a licensed, unimpaired parent or guardian, a licensed or certified unimpaired driver education instructor, or a licensed, unimpaired person at least twenty-five rides in the front seat [A01].
Why it matters: Solo driving is the default for the first quarter year.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec02-F11 | anchor: A02
When one of the qualified supervising adults is in the vehicle with a junior driver, there is no restriction on how many passengers ride along, except that the driver may never carry more passengers than there are safety belts [A02].
Why it matters: Supervision lifts the passenger count limit but not the belt limit.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec02-F12 | anchor: A02
During the second three months on a junior driver's license the holder may begin carrying immediate family members, which the law limits to siblings and parents only [A02].
Why it matters: Immediate family here means siblings and parents, nobody else.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec02-F13 | anchor: A02
After holding a junior driver's license for six months there is no restriction on the number of passengers, but the driver still may not carry more passengers than there are safety belts [A02].
Why it matters: The belt rule outlasts every passenger stage.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec02-F14 | anchor: A02
A Vermont junior driver's license holder becomes eligible for a full driver's license at eighteen only with no recalls, suspensions or revocations during the previous six months, and that six month period starts on the date of reinstatement [A02].
Why it matters: A recall restarts the six month clock from reinstatement.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec02-F15 | anchor: A02
A person with a junior driver's license from another state who applies for a Vermont junior license must prove completion of a state approved driver education course that meets or exceeds Vermont requirements, must pass an eye, written and road test, and stays under the graduated license law unless the other state's license was held for at least six months [A02].
Why it matters: Out-of-state junior drivers face all three tests here.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec02-F16 | anchor: A02
A learner's permit or junior driver's license is a recallable provisional license, and a junior operator caught carrying passengers for hire or driving for an employer receives a ninety day recall [A02].
Why it matters: The two employment related violations both carry ninety days.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec02-F17 | anchor: A02
A recall of thirty days follows a recommendation from a diversion or reparative board, while junior operator point accumulation, meaning a single three point speeding violation or a six point total, brings a ninety day recall [A02].
Why it matters: One three point speeding ticket alone is enough for a points recall.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec02-F18 | anchor: A02
Texting as a junior operator brings a thirty day recall, along with fines of at least one hundred dollars and at least two points on the driving record [A02].
Why it matters: Texting recall is thirty days plus money plus points.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec02-F19 | anchor: A02
While a recall is in effect the person is ineligible for a junior driver's license or a driver's license, and a person whose permit or license is recalled has the right to a hearing [A02].
Why it matters: A recall blocks the next license step entirely.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec02-F20 | anchor: A02
A recalled learner's permit or junior driver's license is restored when its specific term expires and, if required, after the holder passes a re-examination, and no reinstatement fee is due for restoring it [A02].
Why it matters: Restoration is automatic at term end and costs no fee.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec02-F21 | anchor: A03
Motor vehicle crashes are the leading cause of death and injury for teenagers, and a parent or guardian has a critical role in shaping a teen's safe driving habits [A03].
Why it matters: The handbook frames the graduated law around this risk.
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec02-F22 | anchor: A03
The law requires teens from fifteen to eighteen to learn to drive in stages because young drivers are placed at risk by age, lack of driving experience, passengers and other distractions, and the graduated program exists to save teen lives and reduce injuries even though it cannot prevent every teen crash [A03].
Why it matters: The four named risk factors explain each restriction.
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec02-F23 | anchor: A03
The handbook states that more teens in the United States are killed texting while driving than drinking while driving [A03].
Why it matters: A handbook assertion given without a cited study; carried as the handbook states it.
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0023]

Misconceptions:
- A junior driver with a supervising adult aboard may fill every seat and more: false, a supervisor removes the passenger count limit, but passengers may never exceed the number of safety belts.
- Any relative counts as immediate family in the second passenger stage: false, the law names siblings and parents only.
- A recall is a suspension with a reinstatement fee: false, a recalled permit or junior license is restored when the term ends, after any required re-examination, with no reinstatement fee.
- Texting as a junior operator only costs points: false, it brings a thirty day recall, a fine of at least one hundred dollars and at least two points.
- A teen who turns eighteen still must wait a full year to drive for work: false, the employment ban ends at one year or at age eighteen, whichever comes first.

Mnemonics:
- Two for the permit, one on the permit, six before the junior: two clean years to apply, one year holding the permit, six clean months before the junior license.
- Hire and hired, ninety; board and texting, thirty: the recall terms for passengers for hire or employer driving versus a board recommendation or texting.
- Three alone, three with family, then anyone belted: the three stages of junior license passengers.

Glossary:
- Graduated driver's license law: the Vermont law that moves new drivers through supervised permit, restricted junior license and full license stages
- Provisional license: a learner's permit or junior driver's license, which can be recalled for the listed junior operator violations
- Recall: a temporary withdrawal of a provisional license for a set term, restored without a reinstatement fee when the term ends
- Immediate family members: for the second passenger stage, siblings and parents only
- Nighttime driving: driving from thirty minutes after sunset to thirty minutes before sunrise, the period that counts toward the ten night practice hours

Dynamic facts isolated:
- None: every rule in this section is stable handbook law for the pined edition; no officeholder, date or fee amount is carried as knowledge.
